Class View

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingws.gc8.View.View
Direct Known Subclasses:
GuiView, TuiView
public abstract class View extends Object
Base class for every View (TUI /e GUI).

Responsibilities

  • Maintains the list of ViewListener (the network controller).
  • Maintains a blocking queue of incoming NetworkMessage: the network thread inserts messages, the UI thread consumes them.
  • Maintains the "soft" state of the UI: nickname chosen by the user and the last gameView snapshot received from the server.

Threading

The messages queue is a LinkedBlockingQueue (thread-safe). gameView and nickname are volatile: written by one thread (update dispatcher / main loop), read by another (printing).

Lifecycle

The subclass implements run() with its own procedural UI logic (for TUI: initial menu, game phases, etc.).

    • sendAndAwaitUpdate

      protected abstract View.SendResult sendAndAwaitUpdate(Object action)
      Sends an action to the server and waits for a new gameView snapshot (i.e., confirmation that the server has processed it).

      Without this wait, after notifyAllListeners the main loop would see the old gameView (with the turn still belonging to the local player) and redraw the prompt immediately before the server's response arrives — typical race condition when sending and then reading shared state without a barrier.

      Reference identity comparison: the dispatcher replaces gameView with a new GameDTO on each ModelUpdateMessage, so gameView != before signals that the server has responded.

      The before/errorBefore snapshots are taken after notifyAllListeners returns: this minimises the window in which a stale (previous-action) error message could be mis-attributed to the current send.

      Returns:
      View.SendResult.OK on snapshot update, View.SendResult.ERROR on server-side error, View.SendResult.TIMEOUT if the server does not reply in time.

    • clearMessages

      public void clearMessages()
      Drops any messages still queued from a previous session. Called when a session is torn down so that a stale message (e.g. a "connection lost" left behind by the old network pump) cannot surface in the next session.

    • waitForMessage

      protected NetworkMessage waitForMessage()
      Waits (blocking) for the next message from the server. Interruptible: returns null if the thread is interrupted.
